review_notes: Money's GetHashCode now hashes in Rust (std DefaultHasher, low 32 bits): equal amounts hash equally, but the values differ from .NET's, which were randomized per process anyway.

Until Book is ported (U-0005), Book.Snapshot still deep-copies through a BinaryFormatter, which can't serialize the façade's native handle: the Money façade implements ISerializable (cents and currency), and a deserialized Money is a new Rust Money of the same amount. The interface goes with the C# at the retirement.
Plus and Times use wrapping arithmetic, as the unchecked C# did.

U-0005.summary: Port OrderBook.Book to Rust (order_book_rs::book::Book, its orders behind its own Mutex) and turn the C# Book into a façade over the bridge exports order_book_Book_*; Snapshot copies the object graph in Rust instead of a BinaryFormatter round trip. Map its members in rust/symbol-map.toml.
review_notes: Book.Snapshot no longer uses a BinaryFormatter: Book::snapshot deep-copies each order (Order::deep_copy), each order, line and price of the copy a new object. Objects the book shared (a line added to two orders, a Money in two lines) are separate objects in the copy, where the BinaryFormatter kept them shared.
Book keeps [Serializable], but its façade holds a native handle, so a BinaryFormatter can no longer serialize a Book: nothing in the repository does since Snapshot moved to Rust.
Book.Import parses long and int as .NET does in the invariant culture (white space, a sign, ASCII digits), with .NET 6's FormatException and OverflowException messages.
The C# class had only its implicit constructor; the façade declares the same public parameterless constructor explicitly.
